description: fz accepts [if true, do: 1]; Elixir rejects it: 'unexpected comma. Parentheses are required to solve ambiguity inside containers.' (verified with the elixir CLI). Tuples and bitstrings already enforce this through the front door's comma_bound wrap; parse_list_literal's element parsing has no comma_bound wrap, so list elements miss it. Fix: list elements are parsed the same way tuple and bitstring elements are, one rule for every container. Done when: a diagnostic fixture with [if true, do: 1] reports a parse error in Elixir's words (fails first), [if(true, do: 1)] still works, and every existing fixture stays green; any fixture or lib spelling the rule rejects is fixed to the Elixir spelling and listed in the red ledger. One commit.
title: A list literal requires parentheses around a keyword-sugar call, as in Elixir
